author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Nashua sewer customers would pay about $3 more per month on average under a three-year rate proposal that advanced from an aldermanic committee. The plan calls for demand and usage charges to increase 7% each January in 2027, 2028 and 2029.

The committee gave the measure a favorable recommendation to the full Board of Aldermen. City officials said the additional revenue would support wastewater operations, debt tied to combined-sewer-overflow work, other system improvements and required reserves as expenses rise.

Officials also reviewed the system’s outstanding accounts. About $1.7 million in sewer bills was listed as unpaid, though roughly $1 million of that total was current and not yet due. The city has placed about 600 liens connected to overdue accounts, according to the meeting report.

The committee vote was 3-1. The proposal still needs approval from the full board before any increase can take effect. If adopted as presented, the phased schedule would spread the adjustment across three years instead of imposing the full change at once, while giving residents a defined timeline for future bills.
dek: A committee backed three annual 7% increases beginning in 2027, sending the plan to the full Board of Aldermen.
headline: Nashua sewer proposal would add about $3 a month for average user
